result.proposed_fix: In both layers, match the joined name (with spaces removed) against stems anywhere: otp(?![ahlo])|mfa|2 ?fa|tfa|onetime|twofactor|verif|authenticat|cvv|cvc|ccv|token|secret|password|passwd|passcode|pwd, instead of listing prefixes. Replace _CODE_LABEL with: a short all-digit value (3-8 digits) is a code when the joined name, label, placeholder or aria label ends in code or pin (optionally followed by number/num/no), unless it matches postal|zip|post ?code|pin ?code|country|area|promo|coupon|voucher|referral|gift|bar ?code|sort ?code|ifsc|swift. Copy the same patterns character for character into snapshot.js and keep the string-equality parity test. Add a test that joins a prefix list with a stem list (not only the reviewer's names) and checks both field_is_sensitive and real Chromium on tricky_fields.html, plus a list of readable names (hotpot, footpath, spinner, pincode, zipcode, countrycode, promocode, author, account). Correct the AC7 row in A0_QUALIFICATION.md and keep the earlier text as a recorded correction.
result.root_cause: Both redaction layers decide sensitivity by splitting a field name into words and matching \b-bounded stems. _words() (uri_assist/redact.py:44-46, snapshot.js:13) cannot split lowercase run-together names, so every \b-anchored rule in _SENSITIVE_WORDS (\b(mfa|2 ?fa|secret|token|auth)\b, \bone ?time\b, \btwo ?factor\b, \bverification ?code\b) and the short-digit fallback _CODE_LABEL=\bcode\b (redact.py:61, snapshot.js:14) never match them. The only run-together fallback, _RUN_TOGETHER (redact.py:35-41, snapshot.js:12), is a fixed list of prefix+stem combinations (pin/pass/code only after listed prefixes, otp only in listed positions, no token/secret/mfa/2fa/onetime/twofactor/verification/authenticat stems), so any name outside that list leaks: emailverificationcode, mfacode, onetimecode, twofactorcode, 2facode, tfacode, authenticatorcode, authenticationcode, onetimepin, smspin, cardcode, cardverificationcode, authtoken, accesstoken, clientsecret, secretkey.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: 16f75d8 (R1) improved camelCase/ALLCAPS/digit splitting in _words and added a few stems ([a-z]*otp, mpin, tpin, ccv, acct), but kept the word-boundary design, which cannot work on lowercase run-together tokens. 627f6b9 (R2) added _RUN_TOGETHER as a list of prefixes for exactly the 20 names the reviewer cited (its comment says pin/pass/code only after a known prefix), and its tests (R2_SENSITIVE_NAMES, tricky_fields.html r1-r20) check only those same names. The parity test compares the JS and Python pattern strings, which shows they are identical, not that they cover the class. Both repairs patched the reviewer's examples, and no test generated names outside them.
